summary: 📄 PAGE 1 / 40 Expanded Abstract — Foundational Framing & System Thesis Title Biologically Adaptive Radiotherapy Optimization System (BAROS): A Multi-Scale, Phase-Coupled Framework for Precision Radiation Oncology Abstract (Fully Expanded — Page 1 of 40) Modern radiation oncology operates at the intersection of physics, biology, and clinical decision-making, yet its dominant optimization paradigms remain largely geome

Current treatment planning systems (TPS) optimize radiation delivery based on spatial dose constraints and organ-at-risk (OAR) tolerances, without explicitly incorporating the underlying biological heterogeneity of tumor tissues.
This limitation imposes a fundamental ceiling on therapeutic gain: dose escalation is constrained not by tumor resistance, but by the risk of collateral damage to surrounding healthy tissue.

The proposed system—BAROS—integrates voxel-level biological modeling, adaptive control theory, and clinically validated dose computation into a unified architecture capable of optimizing treatment plans in both space and time.
At its core, BAROS reframes radiation therapy from a static optimization problem into a closed-loop, phase-coupled control system .

summary: 📄 PAGE 1 / 40 Expanded Abstract — Foundational Framing & System Thesis Title Biologically Adaptive Radiotherapy Optimization System (BAROS): A Multi-Scale, Phase-Coupled Framework for Precision Radiation Oncology Abstract (Fully Expanded — Page 1 of 40) Modern radiation oncology operates at the intersection of physics, biology, and clinical decision-making, yet its dominant optimization paradigms remain largely geome

Current treatment planning systems (TPS) optimize radiation delivery based on spatial dose constraints and organ-at-risk (OAR) tolerances, without explicitly incorporating the underlying biological heterogeneity of tumor tissues.
This limitation imposes a fundamental ceiling on therapeutic gain: dose escalation is constrained not by tumor resistance, but by the risk of collateral damage to surrounding healthy tissue.

The proposed system—BAROS—integrates voxel-level biological modeling, adaptive control theory, and clinically validated dose computation into a unified architecture capable of optimizing treatment plans in both space and time.
At its core, BAROS reframes radiation therapy from a static optimization problem into a closed-loop, phase-coupled control system .
